approachQuestion.prompt:
Can these shipments be rearranged?

Two lists contain integer item codes. Return true exactly when they contain the same multiset: every code must occur equally many times in both lists.

Constraints: both lengths equal, 1 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; values are opaque comparison keys, so hashing and integer-specific sorting are unavailable. Inputs may be reordered.

Examples: [3,1,3] and [3,3,1] → true. [3,1,3] and [3,1,1] → false.

Choose a valid method that meets the full contract with the least unnecessary work.
constraints: The stated input/output and mutation requirements apply to every option.

options.text: Sort both lists and compare corresponding values.
options.feedback: Equal sorted sequences encode exactly equal multiplicities.

options.text: Compare only the minimum and maximum values.
options.feedback: [1,1,3] and [1,3,3] share extrema but have different counts.

options.text: Compare the sums of the two lists.
options.feedback: [1,4] and [2,3] have equal sums but different multisets.

options.text: For each value in the first list, rescan both lists to compare its occurrence counts.
options.feedback: This checks multiplicities but repeatedly scans both lists for every value; sorting enables a linear comparison after ordering.

feedback.reason: Sorted elementwise equality checks multiplicity as well as membership.
details: Copy and comparison-merge-sort each list, then compare the two ordered copies element by element.
Sorted elementwise equality checks multiplicity as well as membership. For [1,1,2] and [1,2,2], sets agree but sorted arrays differ. Separate copies preserve both supplied lists.
“Sort both lists and compare corresponding values.”: Equal sorted sequences encode exactly equal multiplicities.
“Compare only the minimum and maximum values.”: [1,1,3] and [1,3,3] share extrema but have different counts.
“Compare the sums of the two lists.”: [1,4] and [2,3] have equal sums but different multisets.

“For each value in the first list, rescan both lists to compare its occurrence counts.”: This checks multiplicities but repeatedly scans both lists for every value; sorting enables a linear comparison after ordering.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed revealed method, choose its tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count copies, sorting buffer and recursion stack; exclude caller input and returned output. Comparison merge sort uses a linear buffer; comparisons and moves are constant-time.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) additional space

feedback.reason: Two comparison sorts and one equality scan use linear working storage.
details: Comparison merge sort takes O(n log n) worst-case time; its copied records and merge buffer require O(n) auxiliary space. The recursion stack is O(log n), within O(n). Linear time omits sorting, quadratic time overstates the sort cost; constant space omits the buffer.
